newsitem.title: USA: American Express names Chenault COO.
newsitem.headline: American Express names Chenault COO.

text.p: American Express Co. appointed Kenneth Chenault president and chief operating officer, the credit card and travelers check company announced Thursday, anointing him as its No. 2 executive after Chairman Harvey Golub.

Chenault, a 45-year-old Harvard University-trained lawyer, has been a vice chairman and member of the Office of the Chief Executive at the New York-based company since January 1995. His latest appointment makes him one of the highest-ranking blacks in U.S. business.
The president's office has been vacant since Jeff Stiefler resigned in September 1995.
Golub, who is also American Express's chief executive, said in a statement that he plans to continue in his current position for another seven years until he turns 65.
He said Thursday's announcement "clearly recognised" Chenault as the No. 2 executive in the company and the primary internal candidate to succeed him.

Alfred Edmond jr, vice president and excutive editor of Black Enterprise Magazine, estimated there are only about 10 black Americans in the very top executive positions at the biggest companies. "Ten years ago you were hard pressed to name one or two," he said.

Golub said that as president and chief operating officer, all of American Express businesses will report to Chenault, effective immediately, with the exceptions of the American Express Financial Advisers and American Express Bank. Those two will report to Golub during a transition period and then to Chenault.
Chenault will also be responsible for global advertising and brand management and will replace Golub as chief executive of travel-related services.

Chenault joined the company in 1981 as director of strategic planning. Golub said that since then, Chenault "provided strong leadership as we addressed a number of serious issues" that threatened the company's core credit card franchise.

Other prominent black Americans in the upper ranks of the biggest companies include Richard Parsons, president of Time Warner Inc., Richard Nanula, chief financial officer of Walt Disney Co., and Barry Rand, executive vice president for operations at Xerox Corp.
Edmond said Parsons, Chenault and others are "testing how high the glass ceiling really is."
